2608.23893.title: Provenance Guided Incremental Learning Under Evolving Concept Definitions
2608.23893.paper_summary: Learning systems deployed over long periods must adapt not only to statistical changes in incoming data, but also to revisions of the definitions that generate their prediction targets. Conventional concept-drift methods typically infer such changes from observations or prediction errors, even when the underlying policy, rule, or query has been explicitly modified. This paper studies rule-induced concept shift, where the target-defining concept is revised directly, causing previously stored instances to acquire different semantic labels without requiring any change in their observed data. We introduce a provenance-guided incremental learning framework that compiles consecutive concept definitions into a structured rule delta, traces the changed components through historical provenance, certifies records whose previous labels remain valid, and restricts reevaluation to a localized candidate region. Executable revisions are relabeled automatically, ambiguous cases are handled through selective supervision, and the resulting changes are used for incremental predictor repair. A versioned concept memory further supports recurring definitions. We also introduce RuleShift-Bench, spanning financial, demographic, cybersecurity, and graph-structured data with threshold, predicate, logical, relational, recurring, and mixed concept revisions. Across the benchmark, provenance-guided repair attains 92.3% accuracy and 90.2% Macro-F1 while reprocessing 14.7% of the historical collection and retaining 94.6% of affected records. Its average update latency is 179s compared with 993s for complete relabeling and retraining. The results demonstrate that an explicit concept revision can be exploited as a data-maintenance signal, allowing learning systems to update the supervision and predictive state that depend on the change while preserving knowledge that remains valid.
2608.23893.paper_summary_zh: 長期部署的學習系統必須適應不僅是進入數據的統計變化，還有生成其預測目標的定義修訂。傳統的概念漂移方法通常從觀察或預測錯誤中推斷這些變化，即使基礎政策、規則或查詢已被明確修改。本文研究由規則引起的概念轉變，其中目標定義概念被直接修訂，導致先前存儲的實例獲得不同的語義標籤，而無需對其觀察數據進行任何更改。我們引入了一個基於來源的增量學習框架，將連續的概念定義編譯成結構化的規則增量，通過歷史來源追蹤變更的組件，認證那些先前標籤仍然有效的記錄，並將重新評估限制在局部候選區域。可執行的修訂會自動重新標籤，模糊案例通過選擇性監督來處理，並將結果變更用於增量預測器修復。版本化的概念記憶進一步支持重複定義。我們還引入了RuleShift-Bench，涵蓋財務、人口統計、網絡安全和圖結構數據，並包含閾值、謂詞、邏輯、關係、重複和混合概念修訂。在基準測試中，基於來源的修復達到92.3%的準確率和90.2%的Macro-F1，同時重新處理了14.7%的歷史集合，保留了94.6%的受影響記錄。其平均更新延遲為179秒，而完整重新標籤和再訓練則為993秒。結果顯示，明確的概念修訂可以被利用作為數據維護信號，使學習系統能夠更新依賴於變更的監督和預測狀態，同時保留仍然有效的知識。
